name: Diagnostic_EQN-QUD_1
questiontext:
What is the positive solution of the quadratic equation {{CT:0}} \( =0\)?

[[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
First recall the quadratic formula:
 \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \mbox{For} \quad a\cdot {{CT:1}}^2 + b\cdot {{CT:1}} + c &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  0, \\
 \mbox{We have} \quad {{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4\cdot a \cdot c}}{2a}.
  \end{array}\]
 So our question is to find the positive solution to \({{CT:1}}^2 - 2\cdot {{CT:1}} - 7 =0\) that is we substitute in the formula:
 \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 a &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  1, \\
 b &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  -2, \\
 c &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  -7.
  \end{array}\]
 Giving us:
 \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 {{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - (-28)}}{2}, \\
 &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{32}}{2}, \\
 &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{16\cdot 2}}{2}, \\
 &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{2 \pm 4\sqrt{2}}{2}, \\
 &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  1 \pm 2\sqrt{2}.
  \end{array}\]
 We then see that there are two solutions here (as there is a \(=\pm\) sign) we want the positive solution, and given the other terms are positive that is with the \(+\) sign. So the positive solution is: \[ 1 + 2\sqrt{2}. \]

on_true.feedback: This is the negative solution, not the positive.
